messages:
maya: Heads up — running into a nasty behavior with the Android Kotlin SDK + OkHttp. When the access token expires the Authenticator tries to refresh, but if the refresh fails we get an infinite retry loop and sometimes ANR on slow token endpoints. Sample app repro attached. :panic:

maya: Authenticator looks like this:
```kotlin
class TokenAuthenticator : Authenticator {
  override fun authenticate(route: Route?, response: Response): Request? {
    // trying to call suspend refresh from here via runBlocking 
    val newToken = runBlocking { tokenStore.refreshToken() }
    return response.request.newBuilder().header("Authorization", "Bearer $newToken").build()
  }
}
```

jonathan: Can you paste the full stack? Two quick notes: (1) OkHttp calls Authenticator on an internal thread — blocking it with runBlocking (or any long sync call) can deadlock if that refresh path needs HTTP resources or a dispatcher slot. (2) Returning a request that still gets 401 will cause retry loops. If refresh fails, return null to stop retries.

maya: Stack trace shows repeated 401 -> authenticate() -> new call -> 401 -> ... repeating. I was returning the rebuilt request even when refresh failed (I thought OkHttp would stop). Also the sample did a synchronized token write to SharedPreferences from the same thread.

kevin: This is a combination of issues we've seen in the wild:
- Avoid runBlocking inside Authenticator. Move token refresh to a separate executor or use a non-suspending refresh path.
- Use a token mutex so only one refresh happens, other requests wait for the new token rather than triggering new refreshes.
- Set retryOnConnectionFailure(false) if you want strict control over retries.
Example:
```kotlin
val client = OkHttpClient.Builder()
  .authenticator(myAuthenticator)
  .retryOnConnectionFailure(false)
  .callTimeout(Duration.ofSeconds(60))
  .connectTimeout(Duration.ofSeconds(10))
  .build()
```
Also make sure your Authenticator returns null when refresh fails.

sara: FYI I opened PR that changes the Kotlin SDK's Authenticator helper to run token refresh on a dedicated single-thread executor and to short-circuit re-entrant retries. It also adds an opt-in flag for the quickstart: `enableAndroidAuthFix=true`. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-android/pull/1234 :thumbsup:

android-ci-bot: PR 1234 — integration tests: ✅ build passed, device tests: flaky on API 21 (skipped 1 test) :zzz:

maya: Applying the patch now. One more thing: I noticed streaming completions on Android can close early — our sample's response.body?.byteStream()?.use { } seems to get closed as soon as we post to the main thread, which truncates the stream. Anyone seen that?

jonathan: For streaming you need to keep the InputStream open until you've consumed it fully. Retrofit converters will close bodies for you unless you use `ResponseBody`/OkHttp directly. Best pattern: call `client.newCall(request).execute()` on a background thread and forward bytes as they arrive to your UI, only closing stream when you're truly done. Also watch dispatcher settings — too-low maxRequestsPerHost can block streaming calls behind other short requests.

kevin: Also note okhttp 5 changes some cancellation semantics — if you use coroutine adapters, make sure coroutine cancellation triggers `Call.cancel()` immediately. We added a CoroutineCallAdapter in SDK v0.9.8 that wires cancellation properly. If you see coroutines not cancelling, you may be on an older adapter or mixing okhttp 4 vs 5.

maya: Patch + new adapter applied — initial tests look much better. I'll update the quickstart doc with two notes: 1) avoid runBlocking in authenticators, 2) call `retryOnConnectionFailure(false)` in the sample, and 3) explicitly document OkHttp 4 vs 5 compatibility. Filing a follow-up issue for streaming sample improvements. Thanks all! :raised_hands:
